note: Measured on 2026-09-13 against gameplay-export pack v10 (/mnt/archive/datasets/melee/skirmish-gameplay/v10-snapshot-20260913/fox-bf). Fixed since the prior baseline (26, action_state, on P1's own JumpSquat hit by a Blaster laser): Fighter_ProcessHit_8006D1EC's ordinary reaction dispatch calls ftCo_8008EC90 (ftCo_Damage.c:838), whose own first check (if (fp->x2220_b3 || fp->x2220_b4 || !fp->dmg.kb_applied) { inlineB2(gobj); return; }) skips its entire motion-state transition (ftCo_8008E908 -> ftCo_8008DCE0) whenever the hit's own computed knockback is exactly zero, applying only cosmetic hit-effects instead. Fox/Falco's own Blaster laser has zero growth/base/weight-independent knockback (docs/fox-neutral-special.md), so it always computes exactly this. game::damage::apply_hit now gates its entire victim-side reaction (motion-state transition, velocity, hitstun, hitlag, last_hit_by) on the computed knockback being nonzero, while still applying percent and the attacker's own separate last-move-landed/combo-count bookkeeping (combo::record, unconditional) and gating the attacker's own hitlag alongside the victim's. Confirmed against fox-bf.slp: P1 takes a 3% Blaster hit mid-JumpSquat at frame 26 and stays in JumpSquat, uninterrupted, continuing into its own jump two frames later. 156 frames now match (-123 through 32); the new first divergence is frame 33, field action_state on P4 (expected Dash 0x14, actual Turn 0x12) -- squarely the concurrent fox-fd-2/fox-fd-4 loop's own dash-entry-velocity investigation, so not pursued further here to avoid duplicating or racing that work.
